gen.orderNote: Follows the listed order from idea through votes to presidential action

steps.label: A bill is a proposal
steps.quote: A bill is a proposal for a new law or a change to an existing law.

steps.label: assigned to a committee
steps.quote: Once a bill is introduced, it is assigned to a committee whose members will research, discuss, and make changes to the bill.

steps.label: put before that chamber
steps.quote: The bill is then put before that chamber to be voted on.

steps.label: goes to the other body
steps.quote: If the bill passes one body of Congress, it goes to the other body to go through a similar process of research, discussion, changes, and voting.

steps.label: vote on the same version
steps.quote: Then both chambers vote on the same version of the bill.

steps.label: approve the bill and sign it into law
steps.quote: The president can approve the bill and sign it into law.

steps.label: vote to override that veto
steps.quote: If the president chooses to veto a bill, in most cases Congress can vote to override that veto and the bill becomes a law.
